messages.content: Provide a concise paraphrase of the instruction: 'Put the red cube into the blue tray.' Preserve both colors and the action.
Place the red cube into the blue tray.

A sealed box contains 2 red balls and 3 blue balls. You draw balls one at a time without replacement, meaning each drawn ball is removed from the box and not put back. What is the minimum number of draws that guarantees you will have drawn at least one red ball? Explain the worst-case ordering of colors that makes this many draws necessary, and show why the next draw must be red.

You need to draw 4 balls to guarantee at least one red ball. The worst case is that the first 3 draws are all blue, which is possible because there are 3 blue balls in the box. After removing those 3 blue balls, only the 2 red balls remain. Therefore, the 4th draw must be red, since no blue balls are left. Drawing only 3 balls is not enough, because an unfavorable ordering could give you 3 blue balls and 0 red balls. Thus 4 is both sufficient and the minimum number of draws that guarantees a red ball.

A sealed box contains three green balls and four yellow balls. Balls are drawn one at a time without replacement. What is the minimum number of draws that guarantees obtaining a green ball, regardless of the order in which the balls are drawn? Explain the worst-case ordering and why the next draw must be green.

Five draws are required to guarantee a green ball. The worst case begins with all four yellow balls being drawn first, in some order such as yellow, yellow, yellow, yellow. After these four draws, the box contains only the three green balls. The fifth draw must therefore be green, since no yellow balls remain. Four draws are not sufficient, because an unfavorable ordering could place all four yellow balls in the first four positions, leaving only green balls for later draws. Thus five is both sufficient and the minimum number of draws needed to guarantee a green ball.
Provide a concise paraphrase of the instruction: Move the orange cone beside the purple box. Preserve both colors and the spatial relationship.
Place the orange cone next to the purple box.

A sealed box contains four orange balls and five purple balls. Balls are drawn one at a time without replacement. What is the minimum number of draws that guarantees at least one orange ball, regardless of the order in which the balls are drawn? Explain the worst-case ordering that establishes this guarantee.

Six draws are required to guarantee an orange ball. The worst case begins with all five purple balls being drawn first, in some order such as purple, purple, purple, purple, purple. After these five draws, the box still contains the four orange balls and no purple balls. The sixth draw must therefore be orange, since every remaining ball is orange. Five draws are not sufficient, because an unfavorable ordering could place all five purple balls before any orange ball, leaving the drawer with zero orange balls after five draws. Thus six is both necessary and sufficient to guarantee an orange ball.
